courses.title: Japanese Language — N4 to N3 Conversation and Natural Speech
courses.description: Closes the gap between reading N3 Japanese and speaking and hearing it naturally. Students master the casual speech layer (contractions, sentence-final particles, discourse markers), build a working command of the three-tier keigo system, train listening comprehension at natural conversational speed through shadowing, and learn to express uncertainty, nuance, and emotion with the evidential vocabulary that makes Japanese sound like a native rather than a textbook.

courses.title: Japanese Language — N4 to N3 Vocabulary and Kanji
courses.description: Bridges the gap between JLPT N4 and N3 by building the vocabulary and kanji knowledge the grammar-focused JAPN-101 left open. Students expand from ~300 to ~650 kanji using a radical-mnemonic approach, grow their vocabulary from ~1,500 to ~3,750 words through thematic grouping and spaced repetition, master the on'yomi/kun'yomi prediction system, work through key near-synonym pairs, and develop the skim-scan-dive reading strategy for authentic N3 texts.

courses.title: Japanese Language — N3 Grammar Patterns
courses.description: A systematic study of the grammar patterns that separate JLPT N4 competence from N3 fluency. Covers te-form extensions (ている, てある, てしまう, ておく, てみる, てあげる/くれる/もらう), all four conditional forms (と, ば, たら, なら), passive and causative constructions (including adversative passive and causative-passive), potential form, Japanese relative clauses, nominalizers こと and の, and clause connectors (から/ので, が/けど, のに, たり〜たり, ながら).

courses.title: The Kojiki — Reading Japan's Oldest Chronicle
courses.description: A close reading of Japan's oldest literary work, the Kojiki (712 CE), in Basil Hall Chamberlain's 1882 translation. Students trace the text's cosmological myths, genealogical arguments, and embedded waka poetry — learning to read the Kojiki not as literal history or simple mythology but as political literature with a complex reception history stretching from Motoori Norinaga's 18th-century commentary to the post-WWII rehabilitation of Japanese scholarship.

courses.title: Classical Philosophy — Foundations
courses.description: A survey of Western philosophy from its origins in 6th-century Greece through the Hellenistic schools of Rome. Students read primary texts — Plato, Aristotle, Epictetus, Epicurus — and wrestle directly with the questions these thinkers posed: What is the world made of? What can we know? What makes a life worth living? How do we face death? No prior philosophy background required.

courses.title: Home Coffee Roasting — Lab
courses.description: The hands-on companion to COFF-100. Students roast, cup, and analyze their own coffee across six structured labs, building a personal feedback loop between roasting decisions and cup results. Labs progress from sensory calibration through deliberate defect practice to systematic single-variable iteration.

courses.title: Home Coffee Roasting — Foundations
courses.description: An introductory course in home coffee roasting covering the full arc from green bean to evaluated cup. Students learn the history and culture of specialty coffee, how to select and source green beans, the chemistry and mechanics of the roasting process, equipment options for beginners, and how to taste and evaluate their work systematically. The course culminates in a three-roast capstone project.
